item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q006_ubiquitin_like_function_divergence","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, ubiquitin-related proteins, UBX domains, and Ras-binding domains are not merely three unrelated hits to a generic architecture: they are three separate families inside the same Ubiquitin-like superfamily. The lineage is class d, Alpha and beta proteins (a+b); fold d.15, beta-Grasp (ubiquitin-like); superfamily d.15.1, Ubiquitin-like, SUNID 54236. Within that superfamily SCOPe separates Ubiquitin-related as family d.15.1.1, SUNID 54237; UBX domain as d.15.1.2, SUNID 54250; and Ras-binding domain/RBD as d.15.1.5, SUNID 54263. That same-superfamily placement supports the biologically useful inference of remote homology/common ancestry and a conserved beta-grasp ubiquitin-like core across these domain families, and it can justify fold-level template choice or remote-homology annotation at the domain level when the boundaries and similarity evidence are checked. The useful relationship is not family identity and not identical molecular function: SCOPe keeps UBX and RBD as families distinct from canonical ubiquitin-related proteins. It would therefore be unsafe to transfer ubiquitin-specific covalent modifier annotations, UBX-specific p97/VCP-adaptor behavior, or Ras/Rap GTPase effector binding across all three just because they share d.15.1. Family-level functions and binding partners need family-specific evidence, such as the SCOPe/Pfam cross-references PF00240 for Ubiquitin-related, PF00789 for UBX, and PF00788/PF02196 for RBD, or direct experimental evidence.","evidence_used":["get_scop_service_info: /api/v1/releases/current","search_scop: /api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=Ubiquitin-related&mode=token&limit=20; /api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=UBX&mode=token&limit=20; /api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=Ras-binding&mode=token&limit=20","get_scop_node: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/d.15.1; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/d.15.1/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54237; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54237/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54237/annotations; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54250; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54250/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54250/annotations; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54263; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54263/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54263/annotations","list_scop_children: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54236/children?limit=20","get_scop_domains: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1aara_/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1wj4a1/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1c1yb_/parents","compare_scop_domains: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1aara_/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1wj4a1/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1c1yb_/parents"]}]}
